subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should OpenClaw add a stored per-job and heartbeat provenance contract for elevated scheduled runs, or keep the current provider allowFrom model and document it as the operator boundary?
rationale: This changes the elevated exec security boundary and persisted cron/heartbeat contract; automation should not choose that policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design provenance-backed elevation
options.body: Add explicit scheduled-run elevation provenance so trusted owner-created cron/heartbeat work can run elevated without wildcard-elevating internal event providers.

options.title: Fold into scheduling provenance RFC
options.body: Make issue 71712 the canonical design path and keep this issue as cron/heartbeat elevated acceptance criteria.

options.title: Keep config-only hardening
options.body: Document avoiding `cron-event` and `heartbeat` wildcard elevation when multiple users can write schedules or heartbeat instructions, accepting reduced scheduled elevated capability.

recommendation.title: Design provenance-backed elevation
recommendation.body: Add explicit scheduled-run elevation provenance so trusted owner-created cron/heartbeat work can run elevated without wildcard-elevating internal event providers.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent heartbeat/elevation security history makes this the best available owner signal for the security-boundary decision.
